text:
marta: Heads-up: starting design thread for 'SpikeForge' synthetic generator to repro the kernel-selection perf regression we saw on NV-2 last Friday. Goal: deterministic bursts + phased drizzle long-tail shaping + KV warmup heuristics.

raj: Nice. Can we capture the exact QPS ramp we saw? That regression looked tied to burst->kernel-fallback when average seq len hit ~1.2x normal.

emily: I saved the perf flame and pprof; will paste gist in a minute. Quick thought: add a 'kv_warmup' subphase before the bursts to avoid cold KV evictions that coincide with kernel fallback. :thinking_face:

nate: Agree. Also need to test different batching heuristics: strict time-window vs size-threshold vs adaptive. The regression was specific to adaptive shrinking batch sizes too aggressively during drizzle.

ci-bot: Benchmark run 2026-03-15_03:21 completed — 95th latency spike at 1.8s. Link: https://ci.example/runs/7543 :eyes:

raj: Proposed generator config (rough):
```json
{
  "name": "spikeforge-phasedrizzle",
  "seed": 42,
  "phases": [
    {"type": "kv_warmup", "duration_s": 60, "qps": 200, "concurrency": 50},
    {"type": "ramp", "from_qps": 200, "to_qps": 900, "duration_s": 120},
    {"type": "phased_drizzle", "duration_s": 600, "base_qps": 400, "spike_prob": 0.02, "spike_multiplier": 6, "poisson_lambda": 1.4}
  ],
  "batch_policy": {"mode": "adaptive", "min_window_ms": 5, "max_window_ms": 50, "bias_wait_if_kv_cold": true},
  "apples_to_apples": {"kernel_compat": "pinned"}
}
```

marta: Looks good. Couple notes: make seed deterministic in CI, collect kernel-selector trace (trace.kernel_selector) and instrument a kernel_fallback counter metric + kv_cache_hit_ratio per shard.

emily: We should also have an apples_to_apples toggle to force the same model binary/kernel set across runs so we can isolate routing vs runtime. Set "kernel_compat": "pinned" as shown.

nate: I'll add profiler hooks to capture per-token compute time and memcpy stalls. Also add synthetic prompt-length distribution sampler to match production mix (16, 64, 128 tokens).

raj: Can someone run a short replay + spikeforge with qps=450->900 step over 2 minutes and link results? I want to check cold KV miss rate and correlate with kernel_fallback events.

marta: I'll kick it off and post results here. Command I'll use: 
```bash
./spikeforge --config spikeforge.json --seed 42 --out /tmp/run1 \
  && ./analyze-run /tmp/run1 --metrics kernel_fallback,kv_miss,latency_hist
```

ci-bot: Run scheduled by marta at 4098765450

marta: Started run. ETA ~7m

ci-bot: Run complete. Summary: kernel_fallback=127, kv_miss_rate=0.03, p95_latency=1.2s, p99_latency=2.05s. Full logs: https://ci.example/runs/7550

emily: Interesting: kernel_fallback spikes correlate with KV miss bursts in the logs. Looks like adaptive batcher is reducing batch sizes during drizzle, exposing a rare code path in kernel selector that falls back to slower kernels. Hypothesis: increase min_batch_window or bias batcher to wait when kv_cache_hot==false.

raj: Agree. Next steps: 1) increase kv_warmup duration and ramp up qps more slowly, 2) run strict time-window batcher variant for apples_to_apples, 3) run pinned kernels to rule out dynamic kernel routing. I'll draft the new configs and PR them.

marta: Thanks all. We'll track this on the perf sprint board. @nate can you add the detailed traces and pprof links to the ticket when you have them?
